key_insight: The paper shows how to turn standard neural networks into discretization-agnostic neural operators that work directly with continuous scientific data. This lets models learn functions and physical processes in a way that generalizes better across grid resolutions and simulation settings.
problem_solved: Traditional neural networks are often tied to fixed input shapes or discretizations, making them fragile when scientific data are sampled at different resolutions. This work addresses the need for architectures that can learn operators over continuous function spaces and remain reliable across changing discretizations.
method: Adapt popular neural architectures into neural operators that act on function spaces rather than fixed grids.
Design the model to be discretization-agnostic so the same learned operator can be applied across different resolutions.
Use continuous scientific data to learn mappings between input and output functions for simulation and prediction tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a principled route to build models that are more robust for scientific computing and multi-resolution data. It can improve transferability, reduce retraining across discretizations, and make neural methods more practical for simulation-heavy domains.
